newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch institutions hold assets worth NLG 863.9 bln.
newsitem.headline: Dutch institutions hold assets worth NLG 863.9 bln.

text.p: Dutch institutional investors held assets worth 863.9 billion guilders at the end of the third quarter of 1996, up from 845.5 billion at the end of the second quarter, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
The quarterly CBS survey covers investments held by Dutch pension funds and the country's seven biggest insurance firms.

The CBS noted that for the first time ever, institutions' holdings of both shares and bonds were worth more than their holdings of private loans. The Dutch state and other borrowers have shifted increasingly to public bond issues in recent years, rather than placing private loans with institutional investors.
NOTE - The CBS figures refer to investments of the Netherlands' pension funds and its seven biggest insurers.
